I have been farming this land for 40 years, and I know what works on my 1.5 mu. My children and grandchildren have off-farm jobs, so I mostly manage the field myself these days. At 65, I need to save my back, so I will plant my maize with no-tillage — I learned this years ago from my neighbors, and it works well for summer maize here in Quzhou. The wheat stubble is still on the field, but I will just drill the seeds straight in after the wheat harvest.

I will buy hybrid seed from the local agro-shop. Everyone here uses Denghai varieties, and I trust them. One package per mu is enough — about 1.1 packages. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing, then top-dress with urea when the maize is knee-high. In total, I will use about 22 kg of nitrogen, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. My well gives me reliable water, so I will irrigate twice — once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and again at the big trumpet stage when the ears are forming.

For pests and weeds, I will spray herbicide once after sowing and insecticide twice during the season when I see worms or aphids. That makes three sprayings in total. I have done this many times before, and if the weather is normal, I expect to harvest about 1,100 kg per mu. My family will keep some for eating and feeding the chickens, and the rest we can sell.
